9422d8bb-45c8-4251-9356-4b11479206f9.overview: The endangered Spanish imperial eagle and near-endemic Iberian magpie are the marquee resident draws in the Sierra Morena and Doñana National Park. Andalucía's position at Europe's southern tip creates a massive migration bottleneck, funneling hundreds of thousands of soaring birds across the Strait of Gibraltar twice a year. Doñana's wetlands reliably host greater flamingos year-round alongside seasonal influxes of waterfowl.

Autumn migration begins early for some species. Thousands of black kites and white storks gather at the Strait of Gibraltar, waiting for favorable winds to cross into Africa. Inland, extreme heat continues to restrict resident bird activity to the earliest dawn hours.

Peak autumn migration. The Strait of Gibraltar becomes a massive bottleneck as hundreds of thousands of griffon vultures, booted eagles, and short-toed eagles cross into Africa. Dedicated watchpoints around Tarifa offer virtually guaranteed sightings of massive raptor kettles.

Late autumn migration. The Strait of Gibraltar continues to see heavy southbound traffic, with short-toed eagles and griffon vultures crossing into Africa. In Doñana National Park, the first waves of wintering common cranes and waterfowl begin arriving from northern Europe.

sliderOverview.birding: Clark's Nutcrackers and Canada Jays are reliably seen year-round in Banff's boreal forests, and American Dippers dive in the Bow River. Above the treeline, elusive White-tailed Ptarmigan camouflage against the rocky scree.
sliderOverview.hotSprings: Banff Upper Hot Springs, on Sulphur Mountain, is the highest hot spring in Canada — its 1883 discovery and the ownership dispute that followed directly led to Banff becoming Canada's first national park two years later. The pool runs year-round at 38-40°C.
sliderOverview.auroraChasing: Banff sees the aurora several times a season, though a truly big, sky-filling display is closer to a once-or-twice-a-year event. It's real and worth watching for, just not the near-guarantee that further-north destinations on this list offer.
sliderOverview.mountaineering: Best known for ice — routes from roadside cragging to 2,000-foot WI6 lines — with a season from mid-November into May, plus a summer scrambling and alpine season. The rock is often loose limestone, so most climbers come for the ice; Canmore, not Banff town, is the real climbing hub.
sliderOverview.wildlifeViewing: Grizzly bears, black bears, and bull elk draw wildlife watchers to the Bow Valley and surrounding alpine passes. Elk and bighorn sheep are virtually guaranteed along the roadsides and even within town limits, while moose are occasionally spotted in marshy areas along the Icefields Parkway. Wolves and cougars inhabit the park but remain genuinely elusive.
